meta.title: Friends of Animals · Kindness grown through children’s art
meta.description: An Indian non-profit growing compassion for animals in children and young adults through drawing, painting, craft, writing, photography and film competitions.

announcement.text: Registration is open: {name}. Closes {closes, date, long}.

competitions.title: Competitions you can enter
competitions.lead: Open ones come first. Each card shows who can enter and the next date to remember.
competitions.emptyTitle: Our first competition is on its way
competitions.emptyBody: We are preparing the first FOA competitions now. Each one will appear here with its theme, age groups and dates. Schools can sign up early, so their students are ready on day one.
competitions.moreTitle: More themes are on the way. Past and upcoming competitions are all in one place.

how.title: Two ways in, one fair path
how.lead: Enter through your school or on your own. Either way, your work is judged the same way and you get the same certificate.

why.title: Why we start with children
why.body: Children notice animals everywhere: the dog at the gate, the crow on the wall, the squirrel on the window ledge. When a child draws or writes about one of them, they look closely and think about how it feels. That habit of looking closely is where kindness starts.

gallery.title: A gallery waiting for its first pictures
gallery.lead: We will never show made-up children’s art. These frames fill only with real entries, shown with permission, after the first competition.

frames.painting: A painting of your street’s cat?

impact.title: Numbers we can check
impact.lead: We publish only counts we can check, and we round them down.
impact.emptyBody: Counts appear here after the first competition ends.

stories.title: True stories of kindness from India
stories.lead: Short reads for children and grown-ups, with sources you can check.

donate.title: Help more children take part
donate.body: Gifts pay for competitions, certificates and awareness work. We will publish our accounts so anyone can see where the money goes.
